Mix for the cocktail was done gently by pipetting up and down. • Incubation will be done at 56°C for 15 min, then at 80°C for 15 min. • The 15 min incubation at 80°C will be critical for reversal of cross -links and optimal RNA performance in downstream applications such as real-time RT-PCR. • The lower solution will be transferred into a new 2 ml microcentrifuge tube. • Incubation on ice for 3 min. will be done then, centrifugation for 15 min at 10,000 xg will be done. • The supernatant will be transferred to a new microcentrifuge tube without disturbtion of the pellet (The pellet contains insoluble tissue debris, including cross linked DNA). • DNase Booster Buffer will be added which is equivalent to a tenth of the total sample volume (approximately 16 μl or 25 μl) and 10 μl DNase I stock solution. steps.title: Sample Collection and Grouping
steps.instruction: Collect tissue blocks of ameloblastoma (AB), odontogenic keratocyst (OKC), and dentigerous cyst from the archives of the Oral & Maxillofacial Pathology Department, Faculty of Oral and Dental Medicine, Cairo University (covering the period 2013-2018).

substeps.instruction: Categorize collected blocks into three groups: dentigerous cyst (comparator), OKC, and AB.

steps.title: Histological Confirmation
steps.instruction: Confirm the diagnosis of the collected blocks using standard staining.

substeps.instruction: Cut blocks serially into 5 μm thick sections.
Stain sections with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E).

steps.title: Immunohistochemical Staining for KLK 3
steps.instruction: Perform immunohistochemical staining to assess KLK 3 protein expression.

substeps.instruction: Deparaffinize sections by incubating in xylene three times for 5 minutes each.
Dehydrate slides in 100%, 95%, and 80% ethanol (two changes of 100%), for 3 minutes each.
Block endogenous peroxidase activity by immersing slides in 3% hydrogen peroxide solution for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Wash slides two times with phosphate buffered saline (PBS) for 3 minutes each.
Perform antigen retrieval by dipping slides in 10mM citrate buffer (pH 6.0) and heating to 95-100°C for 10-20 minutes.
Cool slides in the buffer at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Rinse slides in PBS three times for 1 minute each.
Apply one or two drops of ready-to-use prediluted primary antibody KLK 3 to each section.
Incubate slides for 30 minutes in a humid chamber to reduce reagent evaporation.
Wash slides in PBS three times for 3 minutes each.

steps.title: RNA Extraction and Purification
steps.instruction: Extract and purify RNA using RNeasy MinElute spin columns.

substeps.instruction: Place the spin column in a 2 ml collection tube, close the lid gently, and centrifuge for 15 s at ≥8000 x g; discard flow-through.
Repeat the centrifugation step until the entire sample has passed through the column.
Add 1500 μl Buffer RPE to the column, close the lid, and centrifuge for 15 s at ≥8000 x g; discard flow-through.
Add 500 μl Buffer RPE to the column, close the lid, and centrifuge for 2 min at ≥8000 x g; discard the collection tube.
Place the column in a new 2 ml collection tube and centrifuge at full speed for 5 min; discard the collection tube.
Place the column in a new 1.5 ml collection tube.
Add 14–30 μl RNase-free water directly to the membrane, close the lid, and centrifuge for 1 min at full speed to elute the RNA.

steps.title: Real-time Quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR)
steps.instruction: Analyze KLK3 gene expression using the Rotorgene PCR system and SYBR Green Universal Master Mix (2X).

substeps.instruction: Set cycle conditions: 95°C for 10 min, followed by 45 cycles of 95°C denaturation (15 s), 60°C annealing (1 min), and 72°C extension (1 min), with a final incubation at 72°C for 5 min.
Perform quantitative analysis using the 2-ΔΔCT method.
Normalize the relative quantitation value of the target to the endogenous control GAPDH (housekeeping) gene.

steps.title: Data Analysis
steps.instruction: Quantify and statistically analyze the expression data.

substeps.instruction: Measure protein expression (Area percent) using computer image analysis (μm²).
Measure gene expression (Fold change) using the Rotorgene PCR system.
Present data as mean and standard deviation.
Perform ANOVA test followed by Tukey’s post-hoc test for pair-wise comparison between the three groups.

2 II. Introduction: 6a. Statement of the Problem: Ameloblastoma (AB), the most frequently encountered tumor arising from odontogenic epithelium, AB characterized by a benign but locally invasive behavior with a high risk of recurrence. The invasion of surrounding healthy tissues by tumor cells is one of the essential steps in tumor progression. Therefore, Identification of invasive activities in amel oblastomas may be useful to predict their biological behavior (Zhong, Guo et al. 2011).Odontogenic kera tocyst (OKC) remains the most challenging to treat because of its locally -aggressive behaviour and high recurrence potential. OKC was previously reclassified a neoplasm by the 2005 World Health Organization (WHO) Working Group and renamed keratocystic odontogenic tumour. (Slootweg, Chan et al. 2017). Tumor cell invasion is found to be enhanced in -vitro by KLK 1, 3, 10 and 13. KLK 6 also increases E -
cadherin shedding and promotes cell pr oliferation, migration, and invasion. KLK could also cause proliferation of tumor cells. Generally, KLK overexpression in malignant tumors has, paradoxically, been shown to be associated with both favorable and poor prognoses. KLK 4 is known to have a role in the formation of normal tooth enamel, where it functions to degrade enamel proteins during maturation (Simmer, Richardson et al. 2011). Control: Archival blocks of tissue specimens of dentigerous cyst.
